newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks up on foreign buying of blue chip.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks up on foreign buying of blue chip.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed up on Thursday on foreign buying of a highly capitalised blue chip stock in the food and beverage sector, brokers said.
The all share index closed 2.42 points up at 637.22 with price gains outnumbering declines by 22 to 19. Highly capitalised blue chip Ceylon Tobacco Co Ltd rose 1.25 rupees to 35.75.

Turnover was 42.6 million rupees led by foreign buying of 335,700 Ceylon Tobacco. "We had to pay up to source the Ceylon Tobacco quantity," said Manjula Kumarasinghe, a trader at brokerage Jardine Fleming.
Brokers say there was a lack of sellers of stock of companies which saw good profit growth in 1996. Ceylon Tobacco recorded a 21.6 percent rise in profits in 1996.

Plantation companies which are expected to see good growth in 1997 are also the focus of local and foreign investors, brokers said. Tea Plantations Investment Trust Plc, which has raised 10 million dollars in London and New York for investing in Sri Lanka's plantations, said it expected share prices to rise three to four times in the next two to three years due to continuing demand for Sri Lankan tea.
